title: Mint or basil for a small balcony
text:
Mint and basil are the two herbs most people plant first, and they want almost opposite things.
Sun: basil needs at least 6 hours of direct sun a day, while mint does well with 4 hours.
Water: mint likes soil that stays moist, and basil wants the top 2 cm of soil to dry before watering.
Cold: basil suffers below 10°C at night, while mint survives frost and regrows from its roots in spring.
Pot size: mint needs its own pot at least 25 cm wide, and a single basil plant does well in a pot 15 cm wide.
Life span: basil is grown as an annual and usually lasts one season, while mint is a perennial that can live for years in the same pot.
On a balcony that gets only morning sun, mint is the safer choice; on a sunny balcony both will grow.
